post.summary:
AssumeUserIdentity exchanges the caller's cluster-admin credentials for
a Fuzzball user token bound to the target user inside the target
organization. The returned token's JWT carries an `act` claim
(RFC 8693) identifying the calling admin, so all downstream services
and audit records can attribute the action both to the impersonated
user (primary actor) and the impersonating admin (`impersonated_by`).

cluster (enforced by the WithRequireClusterAdmin auth wrapper).

post.summary:
ExitAssumedIdentity ends the calling user's assumed-user session and
returns a fresh admin token for the admin identified in the caller's
`act` claim (RFC 8693). The admin identity is minted from the same
offline-token machinery AssumeUserIdentity uses, so the token carries
whatever cluster_admin the admin currently holds — a permission that
was revoked after the assume-user call will not be restored.
post.description:
Authorization: the caller must present a token that carries an `act`
claim (enforced by the activity, not an auth wrapper — this RPC is
reachable by holders of assumed-user tokens rather than by cluster
admins directly).

rather than being sent a silently incomplete stream.

Named user for volume ownership (resolved server-side to UID).
Mutually exclusive with owner_uid when non-empty.

ownerGroupName.description:
Named group for volume ownership (resolved server-side to GID).
Mutually exclusive with owner_gid when non-empty.

ownerUserUuid.description:
User UUID for volume ownership (resolved server-side to UID).
Mutually exclusive with owner_uid and owner_name when non-empty.

node.description:
node targets the substrate node that performs the creation, by node ID
("ip/port"). Empty lets the cluster choose.

On a node-local provisioner this decides where the volume's data lives:
the target becomes the volume's holding node, and every stage that later
uses the volume is placed there. On any other node-served provisioner the
same storage is reachable from every node, so the target only decides which
node runs the creation and changes nothing about the result.

Rejected for drivers that create through a cloud API rather than on a node:
there is no node to target, so accepting it would report success for
something that did not happen. Which drivers those are is a property of the
driver rather than a fixed list, so it is not enumerated here.

stages.description:
All stage rows matching the request; task arrays and multinode jobs have
one row per rank sharing a single allocation.

priority.description:
Set only for job and service stages whose allocation is still tracked by
the scheduler.

priorityUnavailableReason.description: Reason priority is absent for a job or service stage.

fuzzball.api.v4.DescribeWorkflowStageRes.description: DescribeWorkflowStageResponse is the response for the DescribeWorkflowStage RPC.

definitionIds.description: Definition IDs to consider. Empty considers every definition.

targets.description: Targets for which hardware discovery was started.

fuzzball.api.v4.ExplainAllocationReason.description:
ExplainAllocationReason mirrors the internal scheduler enum. Numbers 10-19
are reserved: 10 was PREEMPTION_INELIGIBLE in an earlier draft and has
been removed; 11-19 are held for Phase E fairshare variants. Do not reuse.

 - EXPLAIN_ALLOCATION_REASON_SERVICE_POOL_AT_CAPACITY: An autoscaled-service replica pinned to a pool that cannot host its index,
so it never places. The replica is held in the pending queue while the
autoscaler refuses to release it, or sits in the ready queue when the pool
shrank after it was released.
 - EXPLAIN_ALLOCATION_REASON_LEASE_GRANT_FAILING: Substrate keeps refusing the allocation's lease grant, so every placement
is rolled back and the allocation returns to the ready queue.

headShape.description:
head_shape is the resource shape of the reservation-holding (head)
allocation — the job being backfilled against.

blockingJobs.description:
blocking_jobs are the running jobs whose completion the backfill
reservation's estimated start is anchored on.

routedClusterId.description:
routed_cluster_id is the cluster running this allocation, stamped by the
scheduler from its own cluster ID (in a federation, the orchestrate cluster
the workflow was routed to). Empty when the cluster has no configured
cluster ID.

fuzzball.api.v4.ExplainBlockingJob.description:
ExplainBlockingJob identifies a running job whose completion the backfill
reservation's estimated start depends on.

token.description: Bearer token to present to the endpoint.

expiresAt.description: Absolute expiry time of the token.

url.description: The endpoint URL the token grants access to (convenience).

fuzzball.api.v4.GetAccountOwnerWorkflows.description:
GetAccountOwnerWorkflowsSummaryDetailsResponse returns workflow details for group owners.
NOTE: "Account owner" refers to group owners (deprecated terminology).

GetAccountOwnerWorkflowsUsersResponse returns workflow users for group owners.
NOTE: "Account owner" refers to group owners (deprecated terminology).

substrateVersion.description:
substrate_version is the version of fuzzball-substrate running on the node,
as reported by substrate itself. Empty when the node has not reported it.

status.description: status is the node's scheduling state.

healthState.description: health_state is the node's health, orthogonal to status.

reliabilityScore.description:
reliability_score is a 0-100 rating derived from active conditions and
attributed job failures. Absent means the node has not been scored, which
is distinct from a score of 0. Matches ListNodeInfo so the same field does
not mean different things on the two responses.

conditions.description: conditions are the typed health findings currently active on the node.

scoreExplanation.description: score_explanation shows the contributions behind reliability_score.

failureTallies.description: failure_tallies are cumulative job failures attributed to this node.

lastHealthReportTimestamp.description:
last_health_report_timestamp is when the control plane last accepted a
health report from this node. Zero when none has arrived.

fuzzball.api.v4.GetStageEventsResponse.description: GetStageEventsResponse is the response for the GetStageEvents RPC.

lastSeq.description:
The position of the last message returned. Pass it back as after_seq to
continue; a transcript is append-only, so a cursor stays valid and a
caller can keep polling forward from where it stopped.

total.description:
Total messages the transcript holds, so a caller can tell whether it has
reached the end without issuing another request that returns nothing.

users.description:
users grants the listed users the permission regardless of which group
they currently have selected. Additive with groups, and ignored when all
is set.

Outside the oneof deliberately: naming a group and a few individuals is
the common case, and a oneof would force a choice between them.

fuzzball.api.v4.GroupAccess.description:
GroupAccess grants a storage permission to groups, users, or everyone.

The name is historical: it also carries users. Renaming it would churn the
generated Go, the TypeScript client and every reference, for no behaviour
change.

pageToken.description: Token to pass as page_token to fetch the next page; empty when no more.

events.description: Events in the order they occurred, oldest first.

nextPageToken.description: Set when more events remain. Pass it back as page_token.

substrateVersion.description:
substrate_version is the version of fuzzball-substrate running on the node,
as reported by substrate itself. Empty when the node has not reported it.

status.description:
status is the node's scheduling state. Closes the long-standing gap where
a cordoned node was indistinguishable from a ready one here.

healthState.description: health_state is the node's health, orthogonal to status.

reliabilityScore.description:
reliability_score is a 0-100 rating derived from active conditions and
attributed job failures.

Explicitly optional: absent means the node has not been scored, which is
not the same as a score of 0. Zero is reachable -- an uncorrectable ECC
error, a fatal machine check and a failing disk together deduct more than
the base -- and that node is the one an operator is hunting, so it must
not be indistinguishable from a node that has never reported.

nextPageToken.description: Token to pass as page_token for the next page; empty on the last page.

fuzzball.api.v4.ListWorkflowsScope.title:
- SCOPE_USER: SCOPE_USER returns workflows for the user within the currently selected group
 - SCOPE_ACCOUNT: SCOPE_ACCOUNT returns workflows for the group (deprecated, prefer SCOPE_GROUP)
 - SCOPE_GROUP: SCOPE_GROUP returns workflows for the entire group

serviceAccountToken.description:
A projected Kubernetes ServiceAccount token bound to the audience the
cluster expects for local authentication. Real tokens are short JWTs
(~1-2 KB); the upper bound below is a generous ceiling, not a target size.

fuzzball.api.v4.MemberRelationship.description:
MemberRelationship identifies the role a user holds within a membership
listing (organization or group). It is only populated by member-listing
responses; it is left unspecified everywhere else a User is returned.

seq.description:
Position in the conversation, contiguous from 1 and assigned by the server.
Ordering is by this rather than by timestamp so it stays total and stable:
two messages in the same clock tick, or a clock that steps backwards, would
otherwise leave the order ambiguous.

model.description:
The model that produced an assistant message; empty for other roles.
Recorded per message because the model can change mid-session, and the
transcript has to show which one said what.

toolCallId.description:
The tool call this message answers, on a 'tool' message. A client rendering
a resumed transcript needs this to pair a result with the request it
answers; without it a reconnecting client cannot reconstruct the exchange.

toolName.description: The tool that produced a 'tool' message.

toolCalls.description:
The calls an assistant message requested, as the provider's JSON array, so a
client can render what the agent asked for and not only what came back.

approval.description:
How a tool call came to run: "auto" when the session's settings allowed it,
"user" when someone approved it, or the decision that stopped it ("denied",
"timed out"). Empty on messages that are not tool results.

untrusted.description:
This result carried content from outside Fuzzball's control plane and
therefore tainted the rest of its turn. Exposed because the PRD requires the
taint to be visible to the user, and a client cannot show what it cannot see.

fuzzball.api.v4.Message.description: Message is one entry in a session transcript.

fuzzball.api.v4.MessageRole.description:
MessageRole is who produced a transcript message. A closed set, so a
renderer never has to guess what to do with an unknown role.

observations.description: How many reports have carried this condition since it was first seen.

fuzzball.api.v4.NodeCondition.description:
NodeCondition is a typed, timestamped health finding on a node. Mirrors the
internal condition; multiple conditions coexist.

previousScore.description: Set for score changes and threshold crossings.

worsening.description:
True when the change moved the node away from health. Recoveries are
recorded too, so a history that only showed decline would be a lie.

action.description: Set for drain, policy and replacement events.

policyMode.description:
The policy mode in force when the event was recorded. Empty for
operator-initiated actions.

allocationsRequeued.description: Allocations requeued by an active drain or an eviction.

fuzzball.api.v4.NodeEvent.description:
NodeEvent is one recorded change in a node's health. Mirrors the internal
event; the external numbering is prefixed per convention.

fuzzball.api.v4.NodeEvent.Action.description: Action names what a policy did, or would have done in observe mode.

fuzzball.api.v4.NodeEvent.Threshold.description: Threshold names the policy rung a score crossing relates to.

fuzzball.api.v4.NodeEvent.Type.description:
- NODE_EVENT_TYPE_SCORE_CHANGED: Recorded for every score change, not only those crossing a policy
threshold, so the sequence of these is the score's full history.

byFaultClass.description:
Counts per fault class, for the classes that had an active condition when
the failure occurred.

Typed rather than a string-keyed map: a map would put a vocabulary of
enum spellings on the wire that freezes on release and has no definition
a client can read, while this reuses the same enum the conditions list
already carries.

faultClass.description:
The condition that was active when the failures occurred. UNSPECIFIED
aggregates failures attributed to the node with no identifiable class.

fuzzball.api.v4.NodeFaultClassTally.description:
NodeFailureTallies are cumulative job failures attributed to a node.
NodeFaultClassTally counts job failures attributed to one fault class.

fuzzball.api.v4.NodeHealthState.description:
NodeHealthState mirrors the internal health enum.

 - NODE_HEALTH_STATE_UNSPECIFIED: No health state recorded. A current control plane does not produce this:
a node record is created as UNKNOWN. Reserved for records written before
health tracking existed.
 - NODE_HEALTH_STATE_HEALTHY: Reporting, no active fault conditions.
 - NODE_HEALTH_STATE_DEGRADED: Operational but exhibiting fault evidence.
 - NODE_HEALTH_STATE_UNKNOWN: No usable telemetry: reports have gone stale, or the node has never
reported at all. A node record is created in this state, so a node whose
extension does not support health reporting reads as unknown rather than
healthy. Distinct from healthy.

A node in this state may not have been scored: reliability_score is 0
both for "never scored" and for a genuine zero. On GetNode, an absent
score_explanation is what separates them.

failureTallyDeduction.description:
Total deduction contributed by attributed job failures, after decay and
the configured cap. Not named "penalty": the failureTallyPenalty config
key is the per-failure rate, and reusing the word for the total makes an
explainability field self-contradicting.

configSource.description:
Where the penalties came from: "default", "cluster", or "definition:<id>".
Two nodes' scores are comparable only when this matches.

fuzzball.api.v4.NodeScoreExplanation.description:
NodeScoreExplanation shows how a reliability score was arrived at, so an
operator can argue with the number rather than just read it.

fuzzball.api.v4.NodeStatus.description:
NodeStatus mirrors the internal scheduler node status. This is the node's
scheduling state and is distinct from its health: a node can be READY and
DEGRADED at the same time.

defaultTtlSeconds.description: Default TTL in seconds for objects in this scope.

id.description: The ID of the organization or group.

digest.description: The blob digest to point to.

ttlSeconds.title:
Optional TTL override in seconds.
- unset: inherit from hierarchy (group > org > cluster > system default)
- 0: no expiration (never purge)
- >0: explicit TTL in seconds

force.description:
Allow replacing an existing ref that points to a different digest.
When false (default), a request targeting an existing path whose content
differs is rejected with AlreadyExists; re-putting the identical digest
remains an idempotent no-op regardless of this flag.

ttlSeconds.description: Per-object TTL in seconds. Absent = inherited, 0 = no expiration, >0 = explicit.

effectiveTtl.description: Effective TTL after hierarchy resolution (vs the per-object override above).

options.title: list of options for the input

backendKind.description:
Backend type. Same rationale as AvailableInstanceType.backend_kind:
no in-list constraint here so a Slurm/PBS/static/CoreWeave cluster can
round-trip an existing policy without the validator turning it away.
The activity layer rejects grants whose (backend_kind, backend_id) pair
isn't offered by any cluster in scope.

fuzzball.api.v4.OrganizationGrant.description:
OrganizationGrant identifies one entry in an org's compute policy: a
substrate-offered SKU keyed by (backend_kind, backend_id). Grants are
cluster-agnostic — federate expands each grant to every matching-kind
cluster that has a definition for the SKU at write time.

Field 1 is reserved because it held cluster_id (string, UUID) in the
v4.2.x shape of this message. Old clients sending cluster_id would
otherwise decode as backend_kind on the new server (same wire type,
silent misinterpretation). Reserving forces old-field payloads to
drop, which surfaces as a clean "backend_kind is required" error
instead of a bogus grant.

backendId.description:
SKU (instance type / machine type / shape), resolved from this cluster's
provisioner definitions.

fuzzball.api.v4.OrganizationRelationship.description:
- ORGANIZATION_ALL: ORGANIZATION_ALL selects both owners and members. Used by list requests to
return everyone regardless of role.

requireUpdatePassword.description:
When true, the password is set as temporary and the user is required to change it on next login.
When false (default), the password is permanent and no forced change is required.

baseCostPerHour.description:
The cluster's list rate before the reading organization's price
adjustment, returned to cluster admins only. Explicitly optional because
absence is the enforcement: a bare double left unset would arrive as a
real-looking rate of 0 for every other caller.

id.description:
Central-config id; becomes provisioner_definitions.definition_id.
Federate callers compose it as "<cluster_id>-<backend_id>", sanitized to
the SpiceDB object-id charset (dots in SKU names become underscores) so
the same id can key grant relationships.

backendId.description:
Cloud SKU name (instance type / machine type / shape / vm size). The
orchestrate constructs the appropriate provisionerSpec from this and its
own configured backend.

olderThan.description:
Delete workflows that reached a terminal state before this instant.
Required: pruning without a cutoff would delete every finished workflow on
the cluster, which is never what an operator means to type.

dryRun.description: Report what would be deleted without deleting it.

limit.description:
Cap on how many workflows to remove in one call. Zero applies the server's
own limit. Pruning is one transaction per workflow, so a bounded batch
keeps a large backlog from holding the database for the length of the
whole sweep.

workflowIds.description: The workflows removed, or that would have been removed under dry_run.

moreRemaining.description:
True when the cutoff matched more workflows than the limit allowed, so a
further call would remove more.

skippedUnauthorized.description:
How many workflows matched the cutoff but were left alone because the
caller has no permission to delete them.

Reported so an empty workflow_ids can be told apart from a cutoff that
matched nothing: on a shared cluster a caller can walk a long stretch of
other people's workflows before reaching their own, and "deleted 0" then
means "none of them were yours", not "nothing is old enough".

fuzzball.api.v4.QueueAllocationSummary.description:
QueueAllocationSummary is the user-facing view of a queued allocation. It
intentionally omits the owner/token/cluster-origin fields carried by the
admin AdminAllocationSummary: the owner is always the caller.

fuzzball.api.v4.RefreshWorkflowTokenRequ.description:
RefreshWorkflowTokenRequest is empty: the bearer token supplies both the
identity and the workflow it is bound to.

expiresAt.description: Absolute expiry time of the returned token.

generatedPassword.title: Only populated when password was auto-generated

workflowId.description: The workflow ID releasing the ref.

accountId.description:
The group (account) ID owning the ref. Set for group-namespace refs.
Exactly one of account_id / user_id identifies the owner, matching the ref.

userId.description:
The user ID owning the ref. Set for user-namespace refs.
Exactly one of account_id / user_id identifies the owner, matching the ref.

warnings.description:
warnings describes what the scan found but deliberately did not act on.

A scan reaches one node, so on a node-local provisioner it sees one node's
storage. Where that disagrees with what Fuzzball has recorded, the scan
leaves the record alone and says so here rather than guessing -- the
operator has context the scan does not.

fuzzball.api.v4.ScoreContribution.description: ScoreContribution is one condition's effect on the reliability score.

clusterId.title: optional cluster ID when submitting jobs from a federate cluster

workflowPriority.description:
submitter workflow priority (default 0; see StartWorkflowRequest.priority).
Lets scoring rank the candidate against the cluster's ready queue with the
same inputs a submission would carry. Not capped by this message, for the
same reason as StartWorkflowRequest.priority: a value above 0 is a
permission the caller either holds or does not, so scoring must be able to
preview the priority the caller is actually allowed to submit.

readyQueueDepth.description: Queue depths sampled at scoring time; consumed by federate routing.

usableCapacity.description:
usable_capacity is an abstract measure of the cluster's schedulable
capacity used to normalize queue depth (currently the count of usable
nodes). Its computation may evolve without a wire change.

clusterId.description:
cluster_id identifies the cluster this score describes (through a
federate, the cluster the workflow would be routed to). Empty when the
cluster has no configured cluster ID.

blockingQueueDepth.description:
blocking_queue_depth counts the ready allocations whose scheduling
priority meets or beats the candidate's — the work that would run before
it. Zero when nothing outranks the candidate (or the cluster predates
this field); consumed by federate routing.

candidateEffectivePriority.description:
candidate_effective_priority is the cluster's scheduler.priority
expression evaluated for the candidate at scoring time. Cluster-local
scale — never comparable across clusters; reported for observability.

fuzzball.api.v4.SecretScope.description:
- SECRET_SCOPE_ACCOUNT: Deprecated: Use SECRET_SCOPE_GROUP instead.
 - SECRET_SCOPE_GROUP: SECRET_SCOPE_GROUP is the preferred name for group-scoped secrets (formerly SECRET_SCOPE_ACCOUNT).

name.description: Caller-supplied display name, unique per owner.

userId.description: The owning user. Sessions are private to this user.

accountId.description:
The group the session currently acts in. A workflow the agent submits is
owned by user_id and visible to this group, so changing it changes what
subsequent actions target -- a user in three groups can work on all three
from one session.

clusterId.description: The cluster the session is bound to.

model.description:
Reference to the model answering this session's turns. Empty means the
caller has not chosen one and the server default applies at the next turn.

gating.description: Standing tool-tier grants for this session.

fuzzball.api.v4.Session.description: Session is one conversation between a user and the agent.

definitionIds.description:
Complete desired set of granted definition ids for this account (group)
on this cluster (replace semantics). Must be a subset of the
organization's current grant set; out-of-subset ids are rejected.

id.description: The ID of the organization or group.

definitionIds.description:
Complete desired set of granted definition ids for this organization on
this cluster (replace semantics). Ids must fit the SpiceDB object-id
charset ([a-zA-Z0-9/_|-=+]); federate-materialized ids are sanitized to
it by construction.

fuzzball.api.v4.StageEvent.description: StageEvent represents a single event in the lifecycle of a workflow stage.

fuzzball.api.v4.StageEventType.description:
StageEventType enumerates the types of events that can occur during stage execution.

 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_STAGE_STARTED: Stage lifecycle
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_WORKFLOW_STARTED: Workflow lifecycle
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_IMAGE_PULL_STARTED: Image pull events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_IMAGE_BUILD_STARTED: Image build events, for an Image stage that builds an image the workflow
defines rather than pulling a ready-made one. The base image's pull, and the
compression of the built result, are reported with the pull and convert
events above, which mean the same thing here.

The base image is on the node and the build has begun.
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_IMAGE_FILE_APPLIED: A file from the definition was written into the image being built.
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_IMAGE_POST_STARTED: The definition's post script started.
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_IMAGE_POST_COMPLETED: The definition's post script finished.
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_IMAGE_CACHE_SAVED: The built image was saved in the object cache under the name the definition
gave it.
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_CONTAINER_STARTED: Container events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_SCALE_UP: Autoscaler emitted a persisted scale-up event for a service replica.
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_SCALE_DOWN: A service replica was scaled down (stopped by the autoscaler/extension).
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_DRAINING: A retiring service replica was deregistered from DNS and is draining
before being stopped.
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_WAITING_ON_DEPENDENCY: Dependencies
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_RESOURCES_ALLOCATED: Resource allocation
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_PROVISIONING_REQUESTED: Provisioning events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_VOLUME_CREATE_STARTED: Volume events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_FILE_TRANSFER_STARTED: File transfer events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_ERROR: Error
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_PREEMPTED: Preemption events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_PRIORITY_SET: Priority events
 - STAGE_EVENT_TYPE_RESERVATION_HELD: Backfill events

effectivePriority.description:
effective_priority is only meaningful when computed is true; the
scheduler recomputes it each tick for ready and running allocations.

priorityExpression.description:
priority_expression is the cluster expression the scheduler evaluates;
the *_priority fields above and create_time are its inputs.

fuzzball.api.v4.StagePriorityDetails.description:
StagePriorityDetails reports the current scheduling priority of a job or
service stage and the inputs used to calculate it.

clusterId.title: optional cluster ID when submitting jobs from a federate cluster

applicationId.title: optional application ID to track application usage stats

priority.description:
Workflow priority input at submission (default 0).

Not capped in the message: the cap is a permission question, not a shape
question, and it is enforced identically here and on
UpdateWorkflowPriority. A submitter is held to <= 0 so nobody can
self-boost above other tenants (FUZZ-7453); an owner of the workflow's
organization may submit a positive value.

preemptible.description:
preemptible indicates whether the workflow's allocations may be preempted
by higher priority allocations. Logically ORed with the definition's
top-level preemptible field; a job or service that sets preemptible
explicitly overrides the workflow-level value.

segment.description:
segment restricts this provisioner to nodes with a matching segment label.
If empty, the provisioner is globally accessible from any node.
Immutable after creation.

local.description:
local declares that this provisioner's path resolves to different storage
on each node, so a volume created on one node is not visible from any
other. Fuzzball then places the stages that use a volume on the node
holding it.

Both kinds of volume take that path. A volume the workflow creates is
placed where its own creation stage ran. A persistent volume is bound
rather than created, so its node is recorded on the volume at creation or
import (storage_volumes.home_hostport) and read back at submission -- a
bind runs no creation stage, so there is no completion event to carry the
answer instead.

A persistent volume with no recorded node cannot be placed. That means
volumes predating the home_hostport column, for which the node was never
written down and cannot be recovered; they are refused at submission
rather than started blind. Same for a recorded node that is not currently
registered: no other node can reach the volume, so the job would wait
indefinitely.

Shapes needing more than one node -- a multinode stage, a task array above
concurrency 1, an auto-scaled service above one replica -- are refused at
submission, because the volume exists on one node only.

Necessary because the distinction cannot be inferred. A hostpath
provisioner at /mnt/shared is correct when that path is a shared mount and
silently wrong when it is not, and the configuration is identical either
way. Fuzzball placed the volume stage and the consuming job on independent
allocations, so on a multi-node cluster the volume was often created on one
node and published on another; where the path was not shared the publish
failed with a bare "no such file or directory" and roughly half of all
workflows on such a cluster failed (FUZZ-8579).

Defaults false, which treats the path as shared and places without
constraint. Turning it on restricts placement, so the operator asserts it
rather than Fuzzball guessing -- a wrong guess in the shared direction
breaks nothing that is not already broken, while a wrong guess in the
node-local direction would needlessly serialize every workflow on a
correctly configured cluster onto one node.

lustreCapacityGbs.description:
OCI Managed Lustre self-provisioning capacity in GB. OCI's minimum is
31200 GB (31.2 TB) across all tiers; valid sizes step by 10.4 TB up to
124.8 TB, then by 41.6 TB. 0 = use default.

lustrePerformanceTier.description:
OCI Managed Lustre performance tier in MBps per provisioned TB. One of
125, 250, 500, 1000. Empty = use default (125).

subPath.description:
sub_path confines every volume on this provisioner to a subdirectory of
the backing share, so that provisioners sharing one filesystem cannot
collide on volume names. Volume names are unique only within a
provisioner, so without it two organizations can each own a volume called
"data" and the driver resolves both to the same directory.

Applies to the hostpath and filestore drivers, which address volumes by
path. Immutable once set: changing it would orphan every existing volume.

The pattern rejects a leading "/", matching the server: an absolute path
would leave the share the field exists to confine volumes to. The other
half of that rule -- no ".." element -- is not expressible in RE2 and stays
server-side, so this pattern narrows the input rather than defining it.

selfProvisioned.description:
self_provisioned records that Fuzzball created this provisioner's backing
infrastructure, and may therefore delete it when the provisioner is
removed. Set by the server, never by the client.

Necessary because self-provisioning writes the resulting resource ID back
into the definition, after which the row is indistinguishable from one that
named an existing resource. Deleting on a wrong guess destroys customer
data, so the distinction has to be recorded rather than inferred.

Absent on provisioners created before this field existed, which are
consequently never torn down -- leaking a filesystem is recoverable, and
deleting someone else's is not.

unsharedPath.description:
unshared_path is a deprecated spelling of `local`. The two named the same
property -- this provisioner's path is not the same storage on every node
-- and were merged into `local` (FUZZ-8983).

Still read, so a provisioner that has not been migrated keeps behaving
correctly: storage.IsNodeLocal() treats either as node-local. Definitions
stored with it set are rewritten to `local` by the unsharedPathToLocal
migration step.

TO REMOVE, in a release after the one that ships that migration -- not the
same one. Definitions live as marshaled protobuf in
storage_provisioners.definition, so once this field is gone the migration
has no accessor to read it and no way to tell which provisioners still
needed rewriting. Removing it means, together:

  - this field, and the regenerated Go, OpenAPI and TypeScript clients
  - the second half of storage.IsNodeLocal(), which becomes GetLocal()
  - the "local and unsharedPath cannot both be set" validation, and the
    "unsharedPath is only supported by the hostpath driver" validation,
    both of which exist only for this transition
  - the deprecation note in the hostpath driver documentation
  - the migration step itself, which has nothing left to find

statusMessage.description:
status_message explains a non-READY status. Without it a failed
provisioner reports only "Error", which is indistinguishable between a
quota limit, a bad subnet and an IAM denial.

Carries a mapped, user-facing summary rather than the underlying error:
several of the failure paths are internal, and their raw text would leak
cloud resource identifiers and SQL into a tenant-visible field.

node.description:
node selects the substrate node to scan, by node ID ("ip/port"). Empty
lets the cluster choose.

A scan reaches one node. On a node-local provisioner that node's storage
is the only storage it can see, so the target decides which subset of the
provisioner is reported -- and, with import, which node's volumes have
their holding node recorded. On a shared provisioner every node sees the
same storage and the target changes nothing about the result.

fuzzball.api.v4.StorageProvisionerStatus.description:
- STORAGE_PROVISIONER_STATUS_PROVISIONING: Self-provisioning of the backing cloud infrastructure (e.g. an OCI
Managed Lustre / FSS filesystem or AWS EFS) is in progress in the
background. The provisioner is not usable for volume operations until it
transitions to READY (or ERROR if provisioning failed).

sizeBytes.description: Volume capacity in bytes (0 = no change). Only set when --size is specified.

lastSeq.description: The last transcript position this stream is known to have delivered.

effectiveTtlSeconds.description: Effective TTL in seconds after hierarchy resolution.

arguments.description:
Arguments is the JSON the model supplied. Present on the call, not the
result.

result.description: Result is the tool's output. Present on the result, not the call.

fuzzball.api.v4.ToolCallEvent.description: ToolCallEvent reports a tool the agent is about to run, or has run.

allowWrite.description: Allow tools that mutate state without running compute.

allowExec.description: Allow tools that run arbitrary cluster compute.

allowDestructive.description:
Allow tools that cancel or delete resources. Note that destructive calls
are always confirmed per call, so this grant alone never suffices.

autoApproveWrite.description:
Run offered write-tier calls without asking first.

Permission has two axes: whether a tool is offered to the model at all
(allow_*), and whether an offered call runs without stopping to ask
(auto_approve_*). One flag cannot express both, because the web surface
offers a tool and then shows an approval card for it.

autoApproveExec.description: Run offered exec-tier calls without asking first.

fuzzball.api.v4.ToolGating.description:
ToolGating is the session's standing permission to call tools above the read
tier, mirroring the four MCP tiers and the `fuzzball mcp serve --allow-*`
flags. Read-tier tools are always available and so have no field here.

These are the session's *standing* grants only. They are not the final word on
whether a call proceeds: a turn that has consumed untrusted content still
requires per-call approval regardless of what is set here.

fuzzball.api.v4.ToolTier.description: ToolTier is a tool's permission tier, mirroring the MCP tiers.

iterations.description: How many model calls the turn took.

stoppedAtIterationLimit.description:
The turn ended at the per-turn round limit rather than because the model was
finished. Ask again to continue.

tainted.description:
This turn consumed content from outside the control plane, so a client can
mark the turn as tainted. Server-side this is TurnResult.Tainted; without it
on the wire a client has to infer taint by scanning messages, which is both
fragile and easy to get wrong.

responseTruncated.description:
A model response hit the response cap and was cut off. Reported for the
same reason as stopped_at_iteration_limit: a client must be able to say the
answer is incomplete rather than present it as finished. Tool calls from a
truncated response are discarded rather than run, so the turn ends here.

fuzzball.api.v4.VolumeSource.description:
VolumeSource distinguishes volumes that Fuzzball provisioned from volumes
that exist outside Fuzzball. The orchestrate activity layer uses this to
decide whether create, chown, and delete operations are sent to the substrate.

UNSPECIFIED is treated as PROVISIONED so old clients and zero-valued fields
default to the Fuzzball-owned semantics.

Legacy v1/v3 volume URI ("volume://<scope>/<class>[/<name>]"). Retained for
backward compatibility with stored catalog values. New producers should set
storage_provisioner_name and volume_name instead.

storageProvisionerName.description:
v4 storage provisioner name (maps to a workflow volume's "use:" field).
Named to match the equivalent field on StorageVolume/VolumeInfoResponse.

accountId.title: account_id is the group ID this workflow belongs to (deprecated naming, represents a group)

workflow priority input; set at submission (StartWorkflowRequest.priority)
and changeable afterwards via UpdateWorkflowPriority

parentWorkflowId.title: ID of the workflow whose token submitted this workflow; empty when user-submitted

version.description:
version defines the version of the workflow document.
Supported versions: "v1" (legacy reference-based volumes) and "v4" (provisioner-based volumes).

volumes.description:
volumes is a map defining volumes to use for this workflow by name.
Map keys define the name of the volume and values are specifications
detailing the data volume. Volume names are used by different
components of the workflow to reference a particular volume instance.

jobs.description:
jobs is a map defining jobs to run as a part of the workflow.
Map keys define the name of the job and values are specifications
detailing the compute job. Job names are used by different components
of the workflow to reference a particular compute job instance.

completed.description: TODO: Remove from public API as this is just an anchor for DAG execution.

annotations.title:
Annotations for the whole workflow. Currently, this is used by the
scheduler to place jobs in a certain topology zone

files.description:
files is a map defining files that may be injected into volumes and jobs.
Map keys define the name of the file and values are the file's contents.
Files names are used by job and volume.ingress components
to reference a specific file.

preemptible.description:
preemptible marks every allocation produced by this workflow (jobs,
services, and internal image/volume/file stages) as eligible for
preemption. Equivalent to `fuzzball workflow start --preemptible`.
An explicit per-job or per-service preemptible value overrides this
workflow-level setting.

images.description:
images is a map defining container images for Fuzzball to build as part of
this workflow. Map keys name the image as it is stored in the object cache
and values define how to build it. A job or service refers to a built
image by its object cache URI, fuzzball://<scope>/<name>, and does not
start until that image has been built.

Image names must be lower case and contain only the characters a-z, 0-9,
'_', '-', '.' and '/'. That rule is enforced in Go rather than by a field
assertion here, because a consuming job's own image URI assertion is
evaluated first and would report the same mistake as an unhelpful "image
URI is invalid" against the job. See validateImageNames.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.description:

layout occurs. Must be one of "NUMA", "SOCKET", or "CORE". An unset

specified, byte is the default. E.g. 32KiB, 1GB, 32GiB.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Defau.description:
Service defines defaults that propagate to all services in the workflow.
These defaults are applied to each service unless the service explicitly
sets a value for the same field. Services do not have a policy field, so
policy defaults are not supported here.

scope.description:
scope selects the object cache namespace the built image is stored in.
Must be one of "user" (the default) or "group".

from.description:
from is the base image the build starts from. It shares the same
semantics as a job's or service's image, so it may name an external
registry (docker://, oras://) or an image in the object cache
(fuzzball://, fb://) -- including one built earlier in this same
workflow, in which case this image is built after that one.

files.description:
files is a map of absolute paths inside the image to the text contents
written there. Files are written after "from" is pulled and before
"post" runs, so the post script can act on them.

post.description:
post is a script run inside the image once "files" have been applied,
with containerized root privileges so that it can, for example, install
packages. "#!/bin/sh" is assumed if no interpreter is specified.

ttl.description:
ttl is how long the built image is retained in the object cache,
expressed as a duration such as "7d", "24h" or "30m". If unset, the
object cache's configured default TTL applies.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Image.description:
Image is a container image built by Fuzzball as part of this workflow from
an embedded definition, rather than pulled ready-made from a registry.

The built image is stored in the object cache under the map key as its
name, in the requested scope, so jobs and services in the same workflow
refer to it as fuzzball://<scope>/<name>. Fuzzball builds it by pulling
"from", writing "files" into it, then running "post" inside it with
containerized root privileges.

name.description:
Used internally to store the job name.  If this field is present in a
definition then it will be ignored in preference for the map key used in
the `jobs` field.

image.title:
Image is the URI to the container image to be used for this job.
Supported uri formats are: "docker://..." and "oras://" for OCI
and SIF(Singularity Image Format) images respectively.
E.g. docker://alpine:latest

command.description: command is the arguments executed by the container process.

env.description:
env is a list of environment variables to be exposed inside of the job
container.

mounts.description:
mounts is a map containing a key that references a volume by name and
value containing a specification with details of how that volume should
be mounted into the job container.

cwd.description:
cwd allows the specification of the the working dirctory used by the job.
This must be an absolute path. If unset the working directory defaults
first to the working directory in the OCI image config if present and
then to "/".

requires.description:
requires is a list of prerequisite jobs/services in the workflow that must be
completed before this job may be started. This allows jobs within a
workflow to be formed into a directed acyclic graph. If requirements
specified by different jobs results in a cycle, the workflow will fail to
start.

policy contains configurable rules that define high level execution
behavior of a job such as max execution time and retries on failure.

task-array.description:

concurrently. This is useful for doing embarrassingly parallel compute
work.

(the top-level `preemptible` field or the --preemptible start flag).
An explicit true or false overrides the workflow-level setting.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.description:
Job is a single compute "step" in a workflow.
There are a variety of different types of jobs that
result in one or more containers being spawned.
By default, a single container is spawned unless the
TaskArray or Multinode fields are specified.

name.description: name is the name of the job to depend on.

Valid values (case-insensitive): RUNNING (Services Only), FINISHED

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.D.description: Dependency is a concrete dependency that must be satisfied before this job can run.

volume.description:

container.

This must match the implementation used by the application within your
job container because different multinode implementations require
slightly different wire up configurations. Must be one of: "ompi",
"openmpi", "mpich", "gasnet", "generic"

within each job container. If not specified, this value defaults to
the number of CPUs allocated to the job container. The total number
of processes spawned for a job can be calculated by multiplying
this value by the number of nodes requested.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Job.T.description:
TaskArray allows a job to be broken up in an embarrassingly parallel
manner for more effective execution. TaskArray jobs are automatically

retry.description:
Deprecated: retry is not implemented and will be removed in a future
release. This field is accepted but ignored.

restart.description:
restart declares whether this step's work can be safely run again from
the beginning if Fuzzball has to take it off a node.

  on-node-fault  run it again elsewhere when a node fault forces it off,
                 and let an operator evacuate it with `node drain
                 --active`. Choose this only for work that is safe to
                 repeat: a rerun starts from the beginning, and Fuzzball
                 does not checkpoint.
  never          never run it again. Work forced off a node is failed
                 with the node and fault recorded against it.

Unset keeps the conservative behaviour: a routine drain leaves the step
running, and a node fault fails it rather than silently repeating work
that may not be safe to repeat.

anything -- activating that field's meaning would change the behaviour
of workflows already in use.

Policy contains configurable rules for the execution of a workflow step.

a scale_up trigger sets `services`, emission of scale events for other

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description: Replicas bounds the number of replicas for an autoscaled service.

metrics_query is a PromQL expression evaluated against collected
metrics; a true (non-zero) result triggers the scaling action.

cooldown-period.description:
cooldown_period is the minimum number of seconds between consecutive
scaling actions.

services lists the services this policy scales instead of the owning
service. Only valid on a scale_up trigger (cross-service bootstrap from
zero): the trigger then emits one event per target service, and the
owning service must not define replicas. Leave empty to scale the
owning service itself. Must not be set on scale_down.

drain-period.description:
drain_period is the number of seconds a retiring replica keeps running
after it is removed from the service's DNS record set, so in-flight
requests can complete before the replica is stopped. 0 means the
default (30). Only valid on scale_down.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description: ScalePolicy defines a PromQL query and cooldown for a scaling action.

triggers.description:
triggers are the independent scale-up conditions, each with its own
query, targets, and cooldown.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description:
ScaleUp is the set of scale-up triggers. Each trigger independently
evaluates its metrics-query (scoped per replica) and, when it fires,
scales its target services — or this service's own replicas when the
trigger sets no services. All triggers of a service must agree: either
every trigger targets other services (cross-service source), or none do
(self-scaling pool).

path.description: path is the destination path of the rendered file inside the container.

services.description:
services lists the services whose addresses are made available to the
script (e.g. service "worker" is exposed as the SERVICES_WORKER array).

script.description:
script is a bash script executed in a restricted interpreter (builtins
only, no command execution or file I/O) whose stdout becomes the file
contents.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description:
DynamicConfig renders a config file from the live IP addresses of other
services and injects it into this service's container.

endpoints.description: Configures fuzzball endpoints to expose a service's functionality.

host.title: Service serves on the host network

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Servi.description:
Network defines if the job should be run inside its own network namespace
and enabled optional exposure of job container ports.
This is required if you want to expose ports from the job container
directly or via port forwarding.

port-name.description: The name of the port defined above to proxy to.

protocol.title:
The endpoint's intended protocol.
Valid values are: http, https, grpc, grpcs, tcp, tls

type.title:
The type of endpoint to create.
Valid values are: subdomain, path
subdomain - creates a subdomain endpoint like myservice.workflow_id.account_id.fuzzball
path - creates a path based endpoint like /endpoints/account_id/workflow_id/myservice

scope.title:
The scope defines who can access this endpoint.
Valid values are: user, group, organization, public
user - only the workflow creator can access
group - anyone in the same account can access
organization - anyone in the same organization can access
public - no authentication required
Default: group (if not specified)

annotations.description:
annotations is a map of key-value pairs carried on the endpoint and
returned by the workflow endpoints API, so clients discovering
endpoints can tell which ones they are meant to consume.

per-replica.description:
Expose every live replica of an autoscaled service pool as its own
endpoint, in addition to the pool's stable endpoint. A replica's
endpoint appears when the replica becomes ready and is removed when
the autoscaler begins draining it, so a gateway that balances across
replicas itself sees one target per replica. Only valid on a replica
pool, and only with type 'subdomain'.

name.description: The name used to refer to this port.

port.description: The port number exposed by the service container.

protocol.title: The protocol used by this port. Valid values are: tcp, udp

uri.description: uri is the uri of the resource to be accessed.

secrets.description:
secrets is a map of key value pairs to use to access resource.
The key specifies the type of data that is being used and the value
specifies raw data or a template for the workflow system to populate with
data internally from the secrets engine.

cache.title:
cache controls ingress caching behavior for this source URI.
Valid values (case-insensitive): once, changed, never

cache-ttl.description:
cache_ttl_seconds sets a custom TTL for auto-cached ingress objects.
If unset (0), defaults to 7 days.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.URI.description:
URI contains the specification for a resource to access as well as
additional data necessary for access such as credentials.

name.description:
Name is the key value of the volume in the volume map containing this
struct. This is normally set internally by client side code when parsing
workflow DSLs, but will need to be set when calling the API directly.

type.title:
type is the kind of volume. This currently determines the lifetime of the
volume and the data contained within it.
Ephemeral volumes are empty upon creation and have a lifespan of the
workflow duration. Upon workflow completion the volume and its data are
deleted. Host volumes represent directories on the shared filesystems of
the nodes themselves. They must be pre-existing and fall under
directories specified in the shared-fs-roots config property of the
Volume service. Must be one of "EPHEMERAL" or "HOST".
Deprecated in favor of reference

ingress.description:
Ingress specifies data that should be fetched and made available within
the volume.

egress.description:
Egress specifies data that exists within the volume that should be
exported to another storage location.

path.title:
Path is specified for host volume types with the absolute path to the
directory to mount.
Deprecated: will be removed

reference.description: Volume reference this volume is referring to.

use.description:
use specifies the storage provisioner name, "ephemeral", or "persistent".
When set, this replaces the legacy reference-based volume resolution.

size.description: size is the requested volume capacity (e.g. "10GB", "1TiB").

annotations.description: annotations is a map of key-value pairs used for provisioner auto-selection.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Volum.description:
Volume is an instance of a data volume used within the scope of a workflow.
There are a couple different types of volumes that have different data
retention behavior. Volumes are the means of managing data for compute
applications to process over the course of a workflow and orchestrate
data movement to bring injest data into the bounds of a workflow for
computation or export data generated from computation it to other storage
locations.

 reserved 2, 5;
 reserved "type", "path";

source.description:
Source is the origin of the data. The type of URIs supported are
determined by whether this is specified under ingress or egress.

destination.description:
Destination is the location to move the data. The type of URIs
supported are determined by whether this is specified under ingress or
egress.

policy.description:
policy contains configurable rules that define high level execution
behavior of a data transfer such as max execution time and retries on
failure.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowDefinition.Volum.description: File specifies details of workflow volume data movement.

serviceName.description: Service (from the workflow definition) exposing the endpoint.

endpointName.description: Endpoint name (from the service network definition).

url.description: Fully-qualified URL clients use to reach the endpoint.

annotations.description:
Annotations declared on the endpoint in the workflow definition. Clients
discovering endpoints use these to tell which ones they should consume.

replicaIndex.description:
1-based index of the pool replica this endpoint addresses. Zero for every
endpoint that is not a per-replica endpoint.

poolEndpointId.description:
Id of the pool endpoint this per-replica endpoint belongs to, so replicas
of one pool can be grouped into a single model. Empty for every endpoint
that is not a per-replica endpoint.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowEndpoint.description:
WorkflowEndpoint is a live workflow service endpoint exposed through the
Fuzzball service proxy.

expirationSeconds.description: Token lifetime in seconds. 0 selects the server default.

name.description: Name of the container to execute the command in.

rank.description: Rank of the container to execute the command in.

name.description: Name of the container to execute the command in.

rank.description: Rank of the container to execute the command in.

priority.description:
The new workflow priority input. Required -- proto3 optional so an
omitted field is distinguishable from an explicit 0, which would
otherwise silently reset a de-prioritized workflow back to the baseline.

Deliberately not capped at 0 the way StartWorkflowRequest.priority is: the
cap is a permission question, not a shape question. A workflow owner is
held to <= 0 so nobody can self-boost above other tenants (FUZZ-7453); an
organization owner may set a positive value, which is the only way to lift
one workflow above a backlog already sitting at the default of 0. The
handler enforces both.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowService.UpdateWo.description: UpdateWorkflowPriorityRequest changes a submitted workflow's priority input.

fuzzball.api.v4.WorkflowStatus.description:
- STAGE_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED: also used for pending
 - STAGE_STATUS_DOWN: STAGE_STATUS_DOWN marks an autoscaled service replica that has been scaled down.

Is the device allocated, only used for fuzzball.substrate.api.substrate.v1.ResourceShowResponse,
this field is ignored when set by a plugin returning DeviceInitResponse
